The output current is 146.6 µA against a 20 µA target, a 633% error. Both mirror legs share the gate bias node `b`, and M1 and M2 both sit at Vgs ≈ 1.09 V. Their currents differ by 7.3×, which matches their width ratio (4.092 / 0.6098 ≈ 6.7×), so the current ratio is set by the width mismatch, not by the bias. M3 and M4 are matched to within 0.7%, so the fault is in the M1/M2 pair. M2 is the element that sets the output current directly, and its sensitivity (+23% error for +20% width) is the largest for the error spec.

M1 is an equally plausible culprit, since shrinking it by the same factor produces the same ratio error (M1 is -20.5%). I rank M2 first because it is the output-leg device that the corrupted ratio most likely came from, and because the 0.61 µm width of M1 is consistent with the 20 µA operating point set by R1 and the input node.
